clause_text: High-risk customers must have their KYC refreshed at least once every 2 years.
Banks shall update KYC records of high risk accounts not less frequently than once in 1 year.
Periodic KYC updation for high-risk customers shall be completed within 3 years.
A suspicious transaction report must be filed within 7 days of concluding that the transaction is suspicious.
The STR shall be furnished to FIU-IND not later than 3 days after the suspicion is established.
Reporting entities shall file the report within 10 days of the conclusion of suspicion.
Customer names shall be screened against the sanctions lists every day.
The entity shall rescreen its customer base against sanctions lists at least once every 7 days.
Screening against UN lists must be carried out within 2 days of any update to the list.
Cancelled foreign exchange derivative contracts shall not be rebooked after these directions come into force.
Rebooking of derivative contracts that were cancelled is not permitted.
Rollover of contracts on maturity may continue to be permitted subject to the Master Direction.
The threshold for taking positions without proof of underlying exposure shall be USD 10 million equivalent.
Positions taken without establishing underlying exposure shall not exceed USD 25 million at any point of time.
An undertaking that the exposure has not been hedged elsewhere must be obtained from the customer at the time of the contract.
Authorised dealers shall obtain a declaration from the user that the same exposure is not hedged with another dealer.
Documents shall be retained for a period of not less than five years.
Records of customer identification must be preserved for at least 2 years after the relationship ends.
Banks may accept originals certified by an overseas notary for foreign portfolio investors.
In case of non-resident Indians, the bank may alternatively obtain a copy certified by an Indian embassy.
These directions shall come into force with immediate effect.
The regulated entity shall display the grievance redressal officer details on its website.
The board of the bank shall review the compliance policy annually and approve amendments.
It shall be the responsibility of the authorised dealer to ensure compliance with these directions.
These directions are issued under section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 and are without prejudice to other permissions that may be required.
Suspicious transactions shall be reported within 7 days and customer names shall be screened against sanctions lists daily.
Rebooking of cancelled contracts shall not be allowed, and the undertaking from the user must be obtained at the time of booking.
